data.narrative:
Spiritus is a Series A climate and energy company founded by Charles Cadieu and Matthew Lee that has raised $41M to date. The frontier-tech climate and energy sector includes one public comparable (LNZA) and eight private peers, though same-stage and adjacent-stage comparables meeting valuation-tier filters remain sparse, limiting peer-median applicability.

Stage-progression methodology is the primary applicable valuation approach. Using total capital raised ($41M) as a proxy for Series A valuation and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of progression to later stages yields an implied valuation of $82M. This method assumes Spiritus's capital efficiency and risk profile align with median Series A-to-later-stage venture performance. The peer universe includes established frontier-energy players such as Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, and KoBold Metals, though direct valuation comparisons lack sufficient narrow-band data points for reliable median extraction.

The triangulation analysis, constrained to a single applicable method, supports a valuation range of $70M (low) to $94M (high), centered on $82M. This range reflects typical post-Series A step-up dynamics but carries material uncertainty given the absence of tightly filtered peer multiples. Key risks include execution risk on capital deployment, frontier-tech commercialization timelines, and regulatory/commodity-price volatility in energy infrastructure. An expanded peer set or additional funding round terms would refine the median estimate.
